full_judgment:
3. Plaintiff's case put in a nutshell are that Wasek Patwari was the owner of suit land in howla interest. Accordingly District Settlement Khatian No. 31 was correctly prepared and published in the name of Wasek Patwari. He died leaving behind four sons namely Asadullah, Chand Mia, Abid Mia and Wakkas Mia, wife Asad Banu, seven daughters namely Maherunnessa, Nesa Bani, Atar Banu, Golap Jan, Tafura Banu, Jahura Khatun, Tafurunnessa as his heirs. Nesa Banu and Tafura Banu sold their share to Aminullah and others. Amin Mia and others sold the said land to Wakkas and Abid Mia, Abid Mia sold his purchased land to Wakkas Mia on 18-1-1927. Wakkas Mia while owing and possessing his inherited and purchased land gifted the same to his daughter on 4-3-1962. The suit land was sold among the co-sharers of plaintiffs and in that process plaintiffs are now owner of 2.02½ acres land. The settlement of the suit land taken by predecessor of the plaintiffs by way of howla interest has been converted into raiyati interest by existing law. The suit land fell in their saham in partition suit No. 53 of 1951 of the Court of Subordinate Judge. During SA operation the same was recorded in the name of predecessor of plaintiffs. They opened holding No. 22 with Tahsil Office and had been paying rent up to 1370 BS. The employees of, defendant No. 1 are not accepting rent from plaintiffs on the plea that Tauzi No. 8 of Superior landlord was sold in auction, which clouded their title Hence the suit. 

 4. Defendant No.1 (Government) contested the suit by filing written statement denying all material allegations made in plaint contending inter alia that suit land is owned and possessed by government. The suit land along with other land appertaining to District Settlement Khatian No. 31 of Mouza."114 of Bara Newazpur, Upazila Begumganj included in Tauzi No. 8. The said land was sold in auction in Revenue Sale Case No. 114 of 1949-50 and government purchased the land in auction and went into possession. Afterward defendant Nos. 2-4 and others took settlement some of lands from Government on payment of salami and rent and possessing the same SA khatian was not prepared in the name of predecessor of plaintiffs. The howla interest of Wasek Patwari was annulled soon after the auction and notice annulling encumbrance was served upon the heirs of Wasek Patwari. The plaintiffs also applied for taking settlement of some of lands from the Government admitting the auction, plaintiffs filed the suit with evil motive. Therefore, suit is liable to be dismissed.
